method: Built-in image_gen; two-pass style transfer of existing 27-object atlas using user reference images.
prompt:
Style-transfer the FIRST input image, an existing 6-column by 5-row atlas of 27 small editorial objects, for the AeroSense iGEM website. Other three inputs are STYLE REFERENCES ONLY (bold flat travel-poster mountain, graphic pixel fantasy postcard, flat toucan illustration). Preserve EXACTLY the original 6x5 cell order, regular gutters, each object's center and extent, and the three EMPTY cells at end of bottom row. Do not combine cells. Final canvas same aspect ratio as first input (1452:1083), high resolution.
Repaint objects as sophisticated bold flat-color editorial illustration, following the third reference's clean large color masses and first reference's angular cuts: restrained five-color palettes per object, strong memorable silhouettes, a few deliberate sharp irregular facets, almost no outline, NO watercolor texture, NO grain, NO stippling, NO gradients, NO realistic gloss/shading, NO thin doodle lines, NO tiny decorative details. Calm cream, sage and deep evergreen for project objects; ochre for team objects; dusty lavender and plum for wetlab objects; muted teal and deep blue-green for hardware/model; warm coral and dark brick for human practices/learning. Preserve the objects' meanings but simplify elegantly. This is editorial art, not scientific data.
Objects ordered row1: fruit fly; fruit fly and grain sack; two conversation bubbles; shared toolkit box; two gears; shield and flask. Row2: notebook; postcard/photos group; clipboard and pencil; two plasmid rings; receptor on a membrane; pipette with four wells. Row3: fluorescent cells in dish; cultured cells; dark reader cube; connected neural nodes; measurement cylinder and ruler; conversation trail with flags. Row4: open book and fly; produce crate with bananas; sprout with circular arrows; four lesson cards; fly sensing molecules; bread with mold. Row5: DNA and cell; colored response matrix; magnifier and grain sack; empty; empty; empty.
Remove the full rectangular paper backdrop from every cell. Genuine transparent background and gutters. Each object may sit on ONE small irregular flat pale patch, not a large square. No external background scene, landscape, people additions, labels, typography, borders, crop marks, drop shadows or watermark. Keep every object entirely inside its own cell with generous transparent padding. Keep the row2 photo-object as a flat postcard illustration; actual member photo assets elsewhere are unaffected.
refinementPrompt: Revise the first illustration atlas to REALLY match the second reference's flat graphic design (toucan poster). Keep the SAME 6 columns, 5 rows, 27 objects and three empty lower-right cells, same aspect ratio and centers. Make this flat vector-like print illustration, NOT a sticker pack, NOT 3D game icons, NOT glossy clip art. Every shape must use a single SOLID color. Eliminate ALL gradients, highlights, glossy spheres, ambient shadows, grain, feathery watercolor edges, white outlines, white edge halos, drop shadows. No glow. No thin veins or strokes on fly wings. Use large quiet asymmetrical shapes, crisp edges and at most 5 colors per object. Wings broad cream shapes, abdomen single ochre with two large dark bands. Use negative space and deliberate cutout shapes like the toucan beaks. Geometric curved silhouettes plus occasional sharp angular facet. Objects should feel like a carefully art-directed mid-century science editorial print. Simplify aggressively: dishes become two simple flat ellipses with flat disks, reader a simple 3-face box, gears three flat colors, notebook 2 broad pages and 4 simple marks. Irregular pale background patches may remain as ONE flat polygon per object with HARD CRISP edges, no brush texture. Genuine transparent background between objects, no full background. No words, no borders, no logos. Retain sage/forest project family, mustard team family, lavender/plum wetlab family, teal hardware/model family, salmon/brick community/learning family. Maintain exactly the original cell arrangement.
scope: Decorative chapter covers and four homepage editorial illustrations. Member cover, people, event photos and scientific media are unchanged.
